clue.text: Diana, one experienced artist, repulsed society

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the letters for one, experienced and artist are read backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
to have met something is to have experienced it
RA, a Royal Academician, is a stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone called Diana, a seasoned painter, rebuffed high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' means driven back: the letters for 'one experienced artist' are turned round, and only then is S added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt, identified with the Greek goddess Artemis.

clue.text: Heathen god in area to betray Ark's resting-place

parts.note: Ra is the ancient Egyptian sun god
to rat on someone is to betray them

explanation.surface: A pagan deity in some region gives away where Noah's boat came to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says Noah's Ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat, the Turkish peak.

clue.text: Island that rises round one Polynesian paradise

indicators.note: the reversed letters go round the numeral for one
in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up, so the word that goes backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An island that climbs around a single South Sea idyll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns THAT into TAHT; 'round' puts I inside it to give TAHIT, and the island's I ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: This island in French Polynesia is famous as a South Seas idyll, painted by Gauguin.

clue.text: Military commander annihilated in gory moment

indicators.note: annihilated means smashed to pieces, so the letters of gory moment are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A general wiped out in a bloody instant on the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Field Marshal Bernard Montgomery commanded the British Eighth Army at El Alamein.

clue.text: Partners at table hiding expression of surprise and disdain

indicators.note: the bridge partners conceal the exclamation between them

parts.note: in bridge, South and North are partners at the card table
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Bridge partners stifle a gasp of shock and contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation like 'gosh'; in bridge North and South play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and disdain are both contempt for something thought unworthy, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Madame going through rubbish finds ring

indicators.note: the abbreviation for madame passes through the middle of the word for rubbish

parts.note: grot is British slang for rubbish or filth

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman rummaging through the bins turns up a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: GROT is British slang for junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a metal or rubber eyelet, a reinforcing ring round a hole.

clue.text: What in music can be represented as sliding?

definitions.text: What in music can be represented as sliding?

indicators.note: the letters of as sliding can be presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: A question about how musical sliding is notated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: glissandi are slides in music, and their letters are those of 'as sliding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissandi are musical slides from one pitch to another, plural of glissando.

clue.text: We feel that news boss is outstanding!

parts.note: ow is what we say when we feel pain
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Staff gush that the newspaper's chief is brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise; here it means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding has not been paid yet, so the money is still due.

clue.text: Male admires frolicking females in sea

indicators.note: frolicking means playing about, so the letters of admires romp into a new order

explanation.surface: A man ogles women playing in the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Mermaids are mythical half-women, half-fish who live in the ocean.

clue.text: Bump from slow boat damaged creel

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

indicators.note: damaged means knocked out of shape, so the letters of creel are rearranged

explanation.surface: A collision with a sluggish vessel wrecked a fishing basket.
explanation.walkthrough: A creel is a wicker basket for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tubercle is a small rounded swelling or nodule, on bone or skin or a plant.

clue.text: Pale when shown alongside feathery layer

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a hen is a feathered bird that lays eggs

explanation.surface: Turning white next to a layer of feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum of feathers but is something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ashen has gone grey-white with shock, like the colour of ash.

clue.text: Old poet wrong about uniform colour

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the words for poet and wrong are read backwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet
evil is wrong in the moral sense

explanation.surface: An ageing poet got it wrong about the colour of a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BARDEVIL round to give LIVEDRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: This brownish green is the shade of many army fatigues, a military colour.

clue.text: One against one not against changes

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters of not against are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement about who opposes whom and who swaps sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is an opponent, someone set against another person.

clue.text: Landowner endlessly seen in retreat

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the Scottish landowner is dropped

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: A landowner forever spotted in a hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a den or hideout, a place an animal or person retreats to.

clue.text: Mint coin — sovereign

parts.note: the penny is a British coin
sovereign as an adjective means royal, of a monarch

explanation.surface: A newly struck coin: a sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' and 'sovereign' both pretend to be about coinage; mint is the herb and sovereign the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a species of the mint family, a herb once used medicinally.

clue.text: Popular player eliminated angrily snatches ball

indicators.note: the rearranged letters grab and hold the ball inside them
angrily suggests the letters of eliminated are thrown about in a rage

parts.note: O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A star footballer, furious at being knocked out, grabs the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angrily' gives MATINEEIDL from ELIMINATED; 'snatches' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee idol is a handsome actor adored by audiences, a popular performer.

clue.text: One spotted in woods: amphibians also reaching lake

parts.note: toads are amphibians
too means also

explanation.surface: A forest creature seen, plus frogs' cousins heading for the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' means seen in the surface, but means dotted with spots in the definition, like a fly agaric.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadstool is a woodland fungus, and the classic red one is dotted with white spots.

clue.text: Fellow consumer?

parts.note: a fellow consumer sounds like another shopper, but read literally it is one who consumes fellows, an eater of other people

explanation.surface: A fellow shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal eats members of its own species, so it literally consumes its fellows.

clue.text: Make quick progress in top set after revision

indicators.note: after revision means reworked, so the letters of in top set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil advances fast in the highest class after exam revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' suggests studying for exams; here it means reworking letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means hurry up or accelerate, as if pressing a car's accelerator.

clue.text: Split the difference with Conservative in dispute

indicators.note: split means opened up, so the word for difference is parted to take a letter

parts.note: an alteration is a change, a difference from before

explanation.surface: Compromising with the Tories in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split the difference' looks like the stock phrase for compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel or argument.

clue.text: Agent provocateur to admit one's easily influenced

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the numeral for one goes inside

parts.note: a plant is a person secretly placed to incite or deceive
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A provocateur confesses that someone is a pushover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admit' suggests confessing; here it means letting in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means pliable and compliant, readily swayed by others.

clue.text: One to raise game becoming winner?

definitions.meaning: on a shoot, a person who drives birds out of cover into the air for the guns
one who beats others, a victor, said playfully

explanation.surface: Someone who lifts their performance turns into a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: On a shoot this person flushes game birds; whimsically, anyone who beats a rival.

clue.text: Scruff last to gamble on tipster's choice

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the gamble's final letter follows the tipster's pick

parts.note: a nap is a racing tipster's strongest recommendation

indicators.note: the final letter of gamble is taken

explanation.surface: A tramp's final bet is on the horse the tipster backs.
explanation.walkthrough: NAP is horse-racing slang for a tipster's best bet of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff of the neck is its back, the same part as the nape.

clue.text: Spring training in extremely effective footwear

indicators.note: the spring and the training go inside the outer letters
extremely means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of effective are used

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
drill is training by repetition, as for soldiers

explanation.surface: Springtime exercise in shoes that work extremely well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes E and E from 'effective'; 'in' puts SPADRILL between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole.

clue.text: A Hebrew beer and where to get it

parts.note: ale is beer
PH is the abbreviation for public house, a pub where beer is sold

explanation.surface: A Jewish man's beer and the place to buy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Hebrew' looks like a person; it means the Hebrew letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, its equivalent of our A.

clue.text: Cold sea mist to envelop drivers in sixty minutes

indicators.note: to envelop means to wrap round, so the hour abbreviation surrounds the motoring body

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour
the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

explanation.surface: A chilly fog closes in on motorists within the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown service for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Haar is a chilly fog that rolls in from the North Sea onto eastern Scotland and England.

clue.text: Prohibition in abundance in state capital

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
galore means in abundance

explanation.surface: Banning drink in a plentiful regional city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now Bengaluru, is the capital city of the Indian state of Karnataka.

clue.text: Ferment's cause found in unknown quarter

parts.note: in algebra Y is an unknown quantity
east is a quarter, one of the four compass points

explanation.surface: The source of unrest discovered in an unidentified district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ferment' suggests unrest in a district; here it is brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that makes sugars ferment into alcohol and carbon dioxide.

clue.text: Shoot dead leaders of revolution at Libreville

parts.note: the late someone is someone who has died

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Gunmen at the head of an uprising in Gabon's capital execute people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a verb about killing; it is a noun for a growth. Libreville is the capital of Gabon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lateral is a side shoot growing from a plant's main stem.

clue.text: Composer with some hesitation put away gun

parts.note: Gustav Holst composed The Planets
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A composer hesitantly lays down his weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To holster a pistol is to put it back in its case on the hip.
